original_question: For a compact Kahler manifold (X, omega), determine whether DMA(X, omega) is convex and whether, whenever phi belongs to DMA(X, omega) and psi belongs to PSH(X, omega), the function max(phi, psi) must also belong to DMA(X, omega).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem stated in the paper: the ambient setting is a compact Kähler manifold (X, ω), the class in question is DMA(X, ω), and the two requested closure properties are exactly the ones asked in the paper—convexity of DMA(X, ω), and closure under the pointwise maximum max(φ, ψ) when φ ∈ DMA(X, ω) and ψ ∈ PSH(X, ω).
missing_details: PSH(X, ω) should be identified explicitly as the set of ω-plurisubharmonic functions on X.

DMA(X, ω) should be defined exactly as in Definition 1.3: φ ∈ PSH(X, ω) belongs to DMA(X, ω) if there exists a Radon measure μ such that for every decreasing sequence φ_j ∈ PSH(X, ω) ∩ C^∞(X) with φ_j ↓ φ on X, the measures (ω + dd^cφ_j)^n converge weakly to μ.
The quantifier in the definition of DMA(X, ω) is universal over all decreasing smooth ω-psh approximating sequences, not merely existential for one approximation.
If one says "DMA(X, ω) is convex," this should be spelled out as: for all φ_0, φ_1 ∈ DMA(X, ω) and all t ∈ [0,1], one has tφ_0 + (1-t)φ_1 ∈ DMA(X, ω).
The expression max(φ, ψ) should be understood as the pointwise maximum.
To remain paper-faithful, no extra assumptions should be added on ψ beyond ψ ∈ PSH(X, ω), and no extra regularity, finite-energy, or local-domain hypotheses should be imposed.
refined_question: Let (X, ω) be a compact Kähler manifold, let PSH(X, ω) denote the set of ω-plurisubharmonic functions on X, and define DMA(X, ω) to be the set of all φ ∈ PSH(X, ω) such that there exists a Radon measure μ on X with (ω + dd^cφ_j)^n converging weakly to μ for every decreasing sequence φ_j ∈ PSH(X, ω) ∩ C^∞(X) satisfying φ_j ↓ φ on X. Is DMA(X, ω) convex, i.e. does tφ_0 + (1-t)φ_1 belong to DMA(X, ω) for every φ_0, φ_1 ∈ DMA(X, ω) and every t ∈ [0,1]? And if φ ∈ DMA(X, ω) and ψ ∈ PSH(X, ω), must the pointwise maximum max(φ, ψ) also belong to DMA(X, ω)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, one may define DMA(X, ω) using bounded decreasing ω-psh approximants instead of smooth decreasing ω-psh approximants; the paper explicitly notes that this replacement is valid and that examples such as φ_j = max(φ, -j) can be used. With that equivalent definition, the same convexity and max-stability question is unchanged.
justification: The draft matches the narrower official problem in the paper, namely Question 6 in §1.1.3, rather than the broader preceding characterization problem Question 5. The official wording on p. 5 asks whether DMA(X, ω) is convex and whether max(φ, ψ) remains in DMA(X, ω) under the hypotheses φ ∈ DMA(X, ω) and ψ ∈ PSH(X, ω). The only substantive additions needed to make your draft fully stand-alone are the paper’s precise Definition 1.3 of DMA(X, ω), the meaning of PSH(X, ω), and an explicit unpacking of what convexity means. The nearby context also explains why the question is framed globally: DMA(X, ω) is distinguished from its local counterpart DMAloc(X, ω), and the authors note known subclasses E(X, ω) and DMAloc(X, ω) before stating Question 6.
